questions.q: What do over-provisioning and under-provisioning a Fabric Capacity have in common?
options: Both come from sizing the capacity based on a one-time guess rather than actual measured behavior
They are both impossible to actually happen in Fabric
Over-provisioning always costs less than under-provisioning
Neither one has any real practical impact
questions.explain: One wastes budget on unused headroom; the other creates sustained pipeline-health problems.

questions.q: What does sustained, daily bursting at the same hour actually signal, according to this lesson?
options: The base SKU is too small for the workload's actual baseline, not just its occasional peaks
The Fabric Capacity is perfectly sized and working as intended
The KQL Database needs a longer retention policy
An Activator rule needs to be reconfigured
questions.explain: Bursting once during an unusual spike is normal; bursting every day means the baseline itself has outgrown the SKU.

questions.q: What is the recommended process for sizing a Fabric Capacity, according to this lesson?
options: Start with a reasonably conservative SKU, observe utilization metrics for weeks, then adjust based on that evidence
Always start with the largest available SKU to avoid any risk of throttling
Always start with the smallest available SKU to minimize cost, regardless of workload
Pick a SKU once at project kickoff and never revisit it
questions.explain: A capacity decision made from real, observed utilization is more reliable than one made from a spec sheet guess.

questions.q: Why is right-sizing described as a recurring check rather than a one-time decision?
options: A real-time pipeline's load changes over time as usage grows and new dashboards or logic get added
Fabric Capacities automatically resize themselves with no human input ever needed
Right-sizing only needs to happen once, at initial deployment
SKU changes are not actually possible after initial provisioning
questions.explain: It's informed by the same observability already built for other reasons (Lesson 52), applied on an ongoing basis.

questions.q: What does an oversized Fabric Capacity typically look like in practice?
options: Running at consistently low utilization, most months, paying for headroom nobody uses
Constantly throttling and building up an Eventstream backlog
Frequently bursting during peak hours every day
Triggering Activator alerts constantly
questions.explain: This wastes the budget Lesson 54 covered, on capacity that's simply never actually needed.
